clue.text: The gaucho overcome by a boxer

parts.note: to cow someone is to overcome or subdue them by intimidation
a boxer is a puncher, someone who throws punches

explanation.surface: An Argentine horseman is knocked down by a prizefighter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overcome' reads as a past participle describing the gaucho, but it is the verb COW, to subdue.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaucho is a South American cattle herder, the counterpart of a North American ranch hand who drives cattle.

clue.text: Food to take round a backstreet

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O
read as 'back street': the abbreviation for street written backwards

explanation.surface: A takeaway meal is carried around a side alley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backstreet' looks like a side alley, but split it: the street abbreviation taken back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: Oats are a cereal grain eaten as porridge, so they are a food.

clue.text: Look noble

definitions.meaning: to look closely, squinting at something
a member of the nobility, a lord

explanation.definitionFit: To peer is to look hard, and a peer is a titled member of the nobility.

clue.text: Figure a local anaesthetic is called for

definitions.meaning: a figure is a numeral or digit

explanation.walkthrough: Read the second sense as 'numb' plus -ER, a thing that numbs, though it is pronounced differently from the figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A figure is a written numeral, and a local anaesthetic is a thing that deadens feeling in one spot.

clue.text: None of his records are modern

definitions.text: None of his records are modern

parts.words: None of his records are modern
parts.note: a writer of chronicles of past times, whose accounts are all of bygone events

explanation.walkthrough: 'Records' suggests music albums, but these are written accounts of history.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer of history records only events of the past, never present-day ones.

clue.text: Exercises in the back-comes a cropper!

indicators.note: in says the exercises go inside the back

parts.note: the back or hindmost part is the rear
PE is physical education, school exercises

explanation.surface: Doing workouts puts a strain on the back, and someone takes a tumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comes a cropper' means falls over, but the cropper here is one who cuts crops.
explanation.definitionFit: A cropper is someone who harvests grain, which is what a scythe-wielding harvester does.

clue.text: Great hotel transformed completely

indicators.note: transformed says the letters of the two words are made over into a new order

explanation.surface: A grand hotel has been totally renovated.
explanation.definitionFit: Altogether is an adverb meaning wholly or entirely.

clue.text: The sound of a babbling brook in North Wales

indicators.note: the sound of says the word for the brook is to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: a rill is a small babbling stream

explanation.surface: A stream gurgles somewhere in the Welsh north.
explanation.walkthrough: RHYL is a seaside town on the North Wales coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhyl is a resort town located on the coast of North Wales.

clue.text: Naturally they expect to make people feel better

definitions.text: Naturally they expect to make people feel better

parts.words: Naturally they expect to make people feel better
parts.note: healers who use plant remedies, so they cure by natural means

explanation.walkthrough: 'Naturally' looks like 'of course', but it means using natural, plant-based remedies.
explanation.definitionFit: Practitioners of plant medicine treat patients with remedies made from plants.

clue.text: A means of ensuring some degree of stability

definitions.text: A means of ensuring some degree of stability

parts.words: A means of ensuring some degree of stability
parts.note: a device that keeps the temperature, measured in degrees, steady

explanation.walkthrough: 'Some degree of stability' sounds like 'a measure of', but the degree is one of temperature.
explanation.definitionFit: A temperature regulator switches heating on and off to hold a set level of warmth.

clue.text: Ring back about one, showing spirit

indicators.note: about says the reversed ring goes around the one
back says the word for the ring is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: an orb is a ring or circle
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Phoning back about something shows enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns ORB into BRO, and 'about' wraps that round I.
explanation.definitionFit: Brio is vigour and liveliness of style, a synonym of spirit.

clue.text: Think to enslave?

definitions.meaning: to ponder or weigh up carefully
read as ..., to undo the freeing of someone

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits as DE (undo) plus LIBERATE (free), so to un-free someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliberate is to consider carefully, and reversing liberation means taking someone's freedom away.

clue.text: Come round, being concerned with insurance

parts.note: RE means about or concerning, as in a letter heading
cover is the protection an insurance policy gives

explanation.surface: Someone regains consciousness while dealing with an insurance claim.
explanation.definitionFit: To come round is to regain consciousness, which is to get well again after fainting.

clue.text: The Right always points to turn around

parts.note: ever means always, as in 'ever hopeful'
S and E are compass points, south and east

explanation.surface: Conservatives always manage to perform a U-turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Right' reads as a political party, but it gives only R.
explanation.definitionFit: To reverse is to go back the other way, a synonym of turning round.

clue.text: Reads to get settled and prepared to eat

indicators.note: settled here means rearranged into a fixed new order

explanation.surface: Someone reads in order to calm down and get ready for dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat that has been cooked in an oven is ready for eating.

clue.text: An old constable or a stripper?

definitions.meaning: a nineteenth-century policeman, named after Sir Robert Peel
something that removes skin or rind

explanation.walkthrough: Peelers were early London police, after Robert Peel who founded the force; the stripper is a tool that removes peel.
explanation.definitionFit: Early police officers were nicknamed after Peel, and a tool that strips rind from fruit is a peeling device.

clue.text: Marked as declared

definitions.meaning: noticeable, distinct, as in a marked limp

explanation.definitionFit: Pronounced means very noticeable, and it is also the past tense of announcing officially.

clue.text: Wheels to turn in class

indicators.note: in says the turned word goes inside the class

parts.note: rate means class or grade, as in first-rate

indicators.note: turn says the little word next to it is read backwards

explanation.surface: A gear wheel needs to spin in its housing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wheels' is the verb here, not the noun; 'turn' acts on the little word 'to', and 'in' places it within the class.
explanation.definitionFit: To wheel is to revolve or spin round, as a flock wheels in the sky.

clue.text: Girls loved him to appear confused, he wrote

indicators.note: confused says the letters of the four words are jumbled together

explanation.surface: A writer was so adored by women that they were bewildered.
explanation.walkthrough: Oliver Goldsmith was an 18th-century Irish writer, author of 'The Vicar of Wakefield' and 'She Stoops to Conquer'.
explanation.definitionFit: Goldsmith was a novelist, poet and playwright, so he is a man who wrote.

clue.text: Lyrical verses by South African on the Black Sea

parts.note: odes are lyrical poems
SA is the abbreviation for South Africa or South African

explanation.surface: Poems written by a South African about the Black Sea coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Odessa is a Ukrainian port city on the coast of that sea.

clue.text: Like a a top man putting questions

parts.note: as means like, in the manner of
a king is the man at the top of a kingdom

explanation.surface: Like a boss, someone conducts an interrogation.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'a' twice; the spare one is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Asking means posing questions, which is inquiring.

clue.text: Mid-evening diner-it's considered more elegant

indicators.note: mid picks the central letter of the following word

parts.note: a diner is an eater, one who dines

explanation.surface: A guest at an evening meal is thought rather smarter.
explanation.walkthrough: The centre of 'evening' is its fourth letter, N.
explanation.definitionFit: Neater means tidier and smarter in appearance, a close synonym.

clue.text: Dicky and Eva have got into a state!

indicators.note: dicky means shaky or unsound, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Someone called Dicky and a woman called Eva have got themselves worked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicky' looks like a man's name, but it means shaky, so the letters of 'and Eva' are shaken up. 'Got into a state' suggests agitation; the state is a US one.
explanation.definitionFit: Nevada is one of the United States.

clue.text: Tried for example getting in scattered seed

indicators.note: getting in says the example word goes inside the scattered letters
scattered says the letters of the word are strewn about

parts.note: say means for example, as in 'a big city, say, Paris'

explanation.surface: A gardener's attempt is scattering seed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scattered' rearranges 'seed' to ESED, and 'getting in' sets the example word inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To essay is to attempt, so essayed means attempted.

clue.text: Arkwright

parts.note: the builder of the Ark in the Bible, read as a wright or maker of an ark

explanation.walkthrough: Arkwright was an inventor of the Industrial Revolution, but split it as ark plus wright, a maker.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the patriarch built the Ark to save his family from the Flood.

clue.text: Beastly /housing — egghead will make personal complaint

parts.note: a sty is housing for beasts, a pigsty
the head of egg is its first letter, E

explanation.surface: An intellectual living in a hovel has a grumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egghead' suggests an intellectual, but it is just the head of 'egg'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid, a minor ailment of one's own.

clue.text: Foreign monsy once held by an Asian nation

indicators.note: held by says the coin's letters are contained within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Old currency is kept in an Eastern country's reserves.
explanation.definitionFit: The anna was a former Indian coin worth one sixteenth of a rupee.

clue.text: Intimidate and there is agitation

indicators.note: agitation means stirring up, so the letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Bullying is happening, and there is unrest.
explanation.definitionFit: To dishearten is to discourage, close to making someone lose nerve.

clue.text: Key agreement for viewers

parts.note: E is a musical key
yes is a word of agreement

explanation.surface: A crucial deal is in the sight of onlookers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' reads as important, but it is the musical key E.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyes are the organs we see with, so they are viewers.

clue.text: Bag in French railway-station may provide somewhere for rubbish disposal

indicators.note: in says the bag is put inside the French station

parts.note: gare is French for a railway station
taken as written
can means may, having permission

explanation.surface: A bag left in a station in France may be put in a bin.
explanation.walkthrough: The French for station is opened around the bag; 'may' then supplies the permission word. Garbage can is American English for a dustbin.
explanation.definitionFit: A garbage can is the American term for a dustbin, a container for refuse.
